nodes.action: pointed DNS at the new cluster before it was ready
traffic hit a cluster that could not serve it
the outage lasted for hours and hit every region
waited for the cluster health check before switching DNS
traffic moved over without a hitch
the API timed out under load
the API held up under heavy load
adopted a stricter policy that also covers the deployment window

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: Hey Kim, got a minute? I need to vent about the cluster migration.

turns.speaker: Kim
turns.text: Sure, what happened? I saw the incident report pop up yesterday.

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: Yeah, so I pointed DNS at the new cluster before it was actually ready. My bad — I thought the health checks were green, but they weren't.

turns.speaker: Kim
turns.text: Oof. So traffic hit a cluster that couldn't serve it? How long did that last?

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: Hours. And it hit every region, not just one. Total mess. We had to roll back DNS manually while the old cluster was still up.

turns.speaker: Kim
turns.text: That's rough. But at least you caught it. What's the fix going forward?

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: I'm going to wait for the cluster health check to pass before switching DNS next time. No more cowboy moves.

turns.speaker: Kim
turns.text: Good call. Also, maybe add a manual approval step in the runbook? I can help with that if you want.

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: Appreciate it. I'll take you up on that later this week.

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: Hey, quick update — the DNS switch finally went clean. Traffic moved over without a hitch this time.

turns.speaker: Kim
turns.text: Nice! So the health check wait paid off?

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: Exactly. And I also enabled autoscaling on the instances, so we shouldn't get caught flat-footed again.

turns.speaker: Kim
turns.text: Good. That should help with the load spikes we saw during the outage. Speaking of load — how's the API holding up? I heard you shipped it without pagination last sprint.

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: Yeah, that was a mistake. The API timed out under load because it was returning everything at once. I added pagination yesterday, so it's much better now.

turns.speaker: Kim
turns.text: Did you test it under heavy load? I don't want another surprise.

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: I did — ran a load test with 10x normal traffic. The API held up under heavy load, no timeouts. Pagination did the trick.

turns.speaker: Kim
turns.text: Great. So we're good on that front. Any other lessons learned?

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: Yeah, I'm adopting a stricter policy that also covers the deployment window — no DNS changes or API releases within 30 minutes of a health check failure. I'll send the doc around.

turns.speaker: Kim
turns.text: Sounds solid. Let me know if you need a second pair of eyes on it.

turns.speaker: Kim
turns.text: Morning, Nate. Saw the postmortem for the cluster incident — looks like you've been busy.

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: Morning. Yeah, I've been tightening everything up. The new policy I mentioned is live now, and it covers the deployment window too, so no more last-minute changes.

turns.speaker: Kim
turns.text: Good. And I noticed the autoscaling metrics look healthy — no more near-misses?

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: Right, the autoscaling kicked in during a spike yesterday and handled it fine. And the API with pagination is still holding up — we had a 5x load burst and it didn't blink.

turns.speaker: Kim
turns.text: That's a relief. So the whole saga ended well, even if the start was rough.

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: Yeah, but I'm not going to forget pointing DNS at a dead cluster anytime soon. The health check wait is now non-negotiable for me.

turns.speaker: Kim
turns.text: Ha, I'll hold you to that. Want to grab coffee and review the runbook changes together?

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: Sure, let's do it. I'll bring the notes.
